summary:
USTR has proposed new Section 301 tariffs on major trading partners over alleged excess manufacturing capacity, with rates for key Asian exporters reaching up to 40 per cent.

title: EU goods trade turns deficit in Q3 2026 as China gap widens
summary:
EU goods trade moved to a deficit in Q3 2026 as imports reached €730.0 billion (~$802.2 billion) and exports €694.0 billion (~$762.6 billion).
Imports rose 15.7 per cent year on year and exports 7.0 per cent; against Q2, they increased 1.7 per cent and 1.8 per cent.
Deficits with China and Norway contributed to the shift; China was the EU’s largest supplier and the US its main export market.

title: Turkiye’s fabric import price falls nearly 32% from 2022 peak
summary:
Turkiye’s average fabric import price was $1.79 per kg in January-September 2026, nearly 32 per cent below the 2022 peak of $2.62 per kg despite volume recovery.
Imports totalled 1.305 billion kg worth $2.335 billion, with China the largest supplier at 419.375 million kg, or 32.11 per cent.
Prices edged up from $1.75 per kg in 2025, while fabric exports reached $625.752 million.

title: Australian wool market extends rally as weaker currency aids gains
summary:
Australia’s wool market rose for a third week in Week 22, with the EMI up 31 cents to 1,769 Au¢/kg amid strong Merino fleece competition and a weaker Australian dollar.
National offerings totalled 28,440 bales; 26,327 were sold and the pass-in rate fell to 7.4 per cent.
Week 23’s forecast 33,250 bales will test demand before the Christmas recess.

title: Indonesia needs stronger productivity to meet 2045 income target: OECD
summary:
Indonesia needs annual growth of 5.8 per cent to achieve high-income status by 2045, but productivity constraints could slow growth to 3.5 per cent, the OECD said. 
It recommended trade and investment reforms, stronger skills, greater female workforce participation and improved governance. 
The OECD projects GDP growth of 5.4 per cent in 2026 and 5.3 per cent in 2027 and 2028.

title: Vietnam keeps US talks amid 35% tariff proposal
summary:
Vietnam will continue US engagement through a Section 301 investigation and talks on a reciprocal trade deal, Luong Hoang Thai said.
The US has proposed extra tariffs of up to 35 per cent on Vietnamese goods, or 20 per cent if the agreement is reached.
Vietnam has supplied information and is preparing firms for 2026-2030 trade risks.

summary:

summary:

A mechanical engineer with international machinery-sector experience, he previously led DIEFFENBACHER Bielefeld.
He will drive growth at the plastics and textile machinery manufacturer, a Barmag–Brückner Group joint venture.

title: Germany's employment edges down after adjustment in October 2026
summary:
Germany had 45.69 million residents in employment in October 2026; the seasonally adjusted total fell 21,000, or 0.0 per cent, from September, Destatis said.
Unadjusted employment rose 95,000, or 0.2 per cent, month on month, below the 2023-2025 October average of 115,000.
Employment was down 224,000, or 0.5 per cent, year on year; adjusted unemployment stayed at 4.1 per cent.

title: India's growth remains resilient amid uncertainties: Goyal
summary:
India's growth story remains strong amid global uncertainties, Finance Minister Piyush Goyal said at the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026. 
He cited 7.8 per cent first-quarter growth, about 12 per cent growth in gross fixed capital formation and $570 billion exports in the first seven months. 
Goyal said India is on track for $1 trillion exports, with EU and US trade agreements progressing.

title: Bangladesh Minister urges RMG factories to reopen from Saturday
summary:
Bangladesh's labour minister has said garment factories are expected to resume production from Saturday after a wage board fixed a new minimum monthly wage for workers. 
The board set the minimum at Tk 17,000 (~$136), up from Tk 12,500 (~$100), after being formed on November 1 amid worker protests. 
He urged workers and owners to keep operations free from disruption.

title: Hong Kong's YGM Trading narrows H1 loss as margin improves
summary:
Hong Kong’s YGM Trading narrowed its first-half net loss to HK$157,000 (~$20,032) from HK$1.597 million a year earlier. 
Revenue fell 16 per cent to HK$66.129 million (~$8.44 million) as garment sales weakened. 
Gross margin rose to 62.9 per cent from 58.5 per cent, while distribution costs fell 20.3 per cent. 
A gain on the sale of a subsidiary also helped narrow losses.

title: Indonesia’s apparel export prices rise 4% in January-September 2026
summary:

Exports totalled $6.760 billion, with the average price at $22.67 per kg, up from $21.78 per kg a year earlier.
The US stayed the top market with a 57.23 per cent share, as 2026 growth shifted towards higher unit prices.

summary:
Bangladesh’s garment industry remained disrupted as workers continued protests, highway blockades and factory attacks, rejecting the proposed monthly minimum wage of Tk17,000 (~$136), a 36 per cent increase from the existing rate. 
Demonstrations across Gazipur, Savar, Ashulia and Narayanganj highlighted workers’ dissatisfaction, with the proposed wage falling short of their demands.

China remained the top supplier at $2.719 billion, ahead of Spain and Bangladesh; all five leading suppliers posted declines.
Trousers and shorts led by product, while cotton and man-made fibre garments together made up nearly three-fourths of classified imports.

summary:
AAFA has welcomed President Trump’s signing of the Customs Notification Act (H.R. 4930), saying it adds protection against illicit and dangerous goods ahead of peak holiday shopping.

summary:
Bangladesh's Minimum Wage Board has proposed a 36 per cent increase in the monthly minimum wage for garment workers to Tk17,000 ($136) from Tk12,500, following negotiations and a vote. 
The proposal awaits labour ministry approval, with implementation expected from December 2026. 
The decision follows weeks of worker protests demanding higher wages amid rising living costs.
